newsletter_capability_detail: Searched the homepage, /product/b2b-company-contact-data, /products/signals (the full 40+ source list with per-source data points), /pricing (signal categories), docs.unifygtm.com developer introduction, Data API overview, 'Connecting your data', and the integrations overview (Salesforce, HubSpot, 6sense, Clearbit, Demandbase, G2, Gmail, Google Tag Manager, Nooks, Orum, PostHog, Segment, Slack). No newsletter publication, Substack/beehiiv source or publication-level editorial field. Adjacent coverage exists - Upriver supplies podcast and creator sponsorship activity, PredictLeads supplies news events - but neither identifies which newsletter publication wrote about a company.
verified_gap: No newsletter publication inventory, no article-to-publication attribution, no sponsor-to-publication pairs and no newsletter momentum, inside a catalogue that already sells the adjacency: 40+ enumerated sources including Upriver's podcast sponsorships and PredictLeads news events, but nothing publication-level in newsletters. Newsletter text could only arrive as customer-pushed custom objects through the Data API.

likely_buyer_role: BUYER of data: sells itself as a vetted wholesale marketplace that licenses specialist providers and resells them on credits, and already licenses a sponsorship-adjacent source (Upriver) plus a news-event source (PredictLeads). The archetype that licenses a newsletter field rather than building a corpus.

contact_route.note: Public support docs with chat entry point; no sales or general inbox published on the pages fetched - the only address on /pricing is security@unifygtm.com, for security matters.

caveats: The 40+ source list ends with 'over a dozen additional sources natively built in', so it is not a closed enumeration - hence Medium confidence on the confirmed gap. Upriver's podcast/creator sponsorship data overlaps part of NF's sponsorship story, so positioning must be newsletter-specific. Custom objects plus the Data API let a customer load newsletter records themselves, but Unify would still have to source the underlying publication data. Open API and webhooks are Business-tier only.
